chunks: 6 - 'Attab ibn Muhammad ibn 'Attab al-Waramini narrated to us. He said: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mufaddal and Muhammad ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Sawwar narrated to us. They said: 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Hakam narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, from Mutrif, from al-Sha'bi. And 'Attab ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Ishaq ibn Muhammad al-Anmati narrated to us, from Yusuf ibn Musa. He said: Jarir narrated to me, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from al-Sha'bi. And 'Attab ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Ayyub ibn Muhammad al-Wazzan narrated to us. He said: Sa'id ibn Maslama narrated to us. He said: Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated to us from al-Sha'bi. All of them reported from his uncle Qays ibn 'Abd.

'Attab said: This is the hadith of Mutrif. He said: We were sitting in the mosque, and 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud was with us. A Bedouin came and said: Is there an 'Abdullah among you? He said: Yes, I am 'Abdullah. What do you need? He said: O 'Abdullah! Has your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) informed you of how many caliphs there would be? He said: You have asked me about something that no one has asked me since I came to Iraq. Yes, twelve -- the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel. Abu 'Uruba said in his hadith: He said: Yes, the number of chiefs of the Children of Israel.

key_terms.اثنا عشر: Twelve -- the number of successors, understood in Shia Islam as the Twelve Imams
key_terms.بني إسرائيل: Children of Israel -- the Israelite tribes, whose twelve leaders are a Quranic archetype
key_terms.خليفة: Caliph/successor -- one who succeeds the Prophet in leadership of the Muslim community
key_terms.نقباء: Chiefs/leaders (singular: naqib) -- the twelve tribal leaders appointed by God among the Israelites

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about twelve caliphs or successors in Islam?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, transmitted through multiple chains converging on al-Sha'bi from his uncle Qays ibn 'Abd, records a conversation in which a Bedouin asked 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud whether the Prophet (s) had specified the number of caliphs who would succeed him. Ibn Mas'ud confirmed the number as twelve, equating them to the twelve chiefs (nuqaba) of the Children of Israel mentioned in the Quran (5:12). For Shia Muslims, this is a key proof-text supporting the doctrine of the Twelve Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt.
